newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: BUPA Ireland says confident of legality of plans.
newsitem.headline: BUPA Ireland says confident of legality of plans.

text.p: BUPA Ireland's chief executive Martin O'Rourke said on Friday that he was absolutely confident about the legality of the company's health insurance plans, Irish state broadcaster RTE said.
O'Rourke's comments followed a report that Ireland's Attorney General advised the government that some of the company's health insurance plans might be in breach of community rating legislation.
Community rating legislation is designed to prevent companies penalising older people or those more prone to illness by charging them more.
Ireland's health ministry declined to comment on the reports but a spokeswoman said they were holding discussions with BUPA about the plans and looking for clarification.

British-owned BUPA entered the Irish market in November, providing direct competition to the state-controlled Voluntary Health Insurance (VHI) which had enjoyed a 40-year monopoly in the Irish health insurance market.
